issues.legal_issue: A suit for a management scheme is not the proper proceeding to determine disputed title to property, particularly where affected transferees are absent.
material_facts: The proposed scheme listed properties in two schedules and included other property later found by a competent court to belong to the deities.
The parties disputed whether additional land belonged to the deities or had been granted to the shebaits.
Most of the disputed land had passed to transferees who were not parties to the scheme proceedings.
A declaration of title to the land in earlier litigation had been set aside because affected transferees were not parties.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to require the disputed land to be specifically listed in the scheme. The existing provision was sufficient, and title to the land could be established in appropriate proceedings without affecting absent transferees' rights.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure to settle a scheme for management of a temple, it is inappropriate to investigate disputed questions of title. A declaratory decree should not be made when persons whose rights would be affected are absent; the Court relied on the earlier decision in Iswari Kalimata v. Manager, Bijni Raj Court of Wards Estate, reported at 1949 (2) ILR (Cal) 587 and 1952 AIR (Cal) 387.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.disputed_property_title: The parties dispute whether particular property belongs to the religious endowment.
predicates.affected_transferees_absent: People who received the disputed property and whose rights could be affected are not parties to the proceeding.

issues.definition: When a management-scheme proceeding involves disputed property title and affected transferees are absent, the title question is left for separate proceedings.

issues.legal_issue: Longstanding service as shebaits and unchallenged shebait rights can justify their continued inclusion in temple management despite a dispute about their legal status.
material_facts: The present shebaits and their predecessors had performed the functions of shebaits for a long period.
Their rights to act as shebaits had not previously been called into question.
It was argued that only a sanyasi could be a de jure shebait and that the present shebaits were only de facto shebaits.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention that the shebaits should be completely excluded from management.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the longstanding exercise of shebait functions and the absence of any earlier challenge to those rights as material. It did not accept that the asserted distinction between de jure and de facto shebaits required their complete exclusion.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.longstanding_shebait_service: The persons concerned and their predecessors have performed the functions of shebaits for a long period.
predicates.shebait_rights_unchallenged: The right of those persons to act as shebaits has not previously been called into question.

issues.definition: In a management-scheme proceeding, longstanding service as shebaits and unchallenged shebait rights support their continued inclusion in management.

issues.legal_issue: Alleged alienation of endowment property is not a basis for excluding shebaits from management when deciding the scheme would require the court to determine disputed title.
material_facts: It was argued that the shebaits and their predecessors had alienated endowment property and should therefore have no share in management.
Whether the alleged alienated property belonged to the deity was disputed.
The Court considered it inappropriate to determine title to that property in the scheme proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the contention that the alleged alienations required the shebaits' exclusion from management in these proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: A court settling a management scheme should not determine disputed questions of title to property in order to resolve an objection to a person's participation in management. The Court applied its conclusion that title questions were inappropriate for determination in the Section 92 Code of Civil Procedure proceeding.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.alleged_endowment_alienations: It is alleged that persons involved in management have transferred property said to belong to the endowment.
predicates.ownership_disputed: The parties dispute whether the transferred property belonged to the endowment.

issues.definition: When alleged transfers concern property whose ownership is disputed in a management-scheme proceeding, the allegations do not require exclusion from management in that proceeding.

issues.legal_issue: A management committee should not be dominated by shebaits when a smaller shebait representation and a majority of outside members can be provided.
material_facts: The proposed committee had eighteen members, twelve of whom were to be selected from the shebaits and six of whom were outsiders.
There were five groups of shebaits.
The Court considered five shebait members sufficient and retained six outside members, reducing the committee to eleven members.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed a committee of eleven members, with five shebait members and six outside members, and required changes to the scheme to reflect that composition.
issues.legal_principle: The Court considered it sufficient to allow each of the five shebait groups representation through one member and held that the majority of the committee should be outside the body of shebaits.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.shebaits_overrepresented: The proposed management committee gives the shebaits a disproportionately large share of its membership.
predicates.multiple_shebait_groups: The shebaits are organized into more than one group.

issues.definition: When a management scheme overrepresents multiple groups of shebaits on the committee, outside members should form the committee's majority.

issues.legal_issue: Shebaits who perform worship and incur expenses in managing the endowment are not merely pujaris and may receive appropriate reimbursement and remuneration under the scheme.
material_facts: The scheme provided for a shebait performing worship to receive a share of cash offerings.
The shebaits performed the worship and incurred expenses for the deity's worship and service.
The shebaits and their predecessors had also managed the property.
The High Court was considered better placed to assess appropriate recompense in light of local circumstances.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the scheme's provision for reimbursement and remuneration to the shebaits.
issues.legal_principle: A shebait is a human ministrant of the deity, whereas a pujari is appointed to conduct worship and is a servant of the shebait. Shebaitship is not merely an office but is also property. A shebait who performs service and incurs expenses is entitled to appropriate reimbursement and remuneration; the Court referred to Mukherjea J.'s Tagore Law Lectures on Hindu Law of Religious and Charitable Trusts and deferred to the High Court's assessment of the proper recompense in the circumstances.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.shebaits_manage_endowment: The persons concerned perform management functions for the religious endowment in addition to arranging worship.
predicates.worship_expenses_incurred: The persons concerned incur expenses in performing worship and service for the deity.

issues.definition: When shebaits manage the endowment and incur expenses for worship, they are entitled to reimbursement and remuneration for their service.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme should permit an application to the court for alteration, modification, or addition to its provisions.
material_facts: The scheme did not provide for an application to the District Judge to address matters arising under the scheme.
Counsel agreed that such a provision should be included.
The Court directed that a provision allowing applications to alter, modify, or add to the scheme be inserted.
issues.conclusion: The Court directed that a clause be added allowing the scheme to be altered, modified, or added to on application to the District Judge.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the practice of providing a mechanism for applications concerning a scheme and referred to Sevak Kirpashankar Daji v. Gopalrao Manohar, 15 Bom. L.R. 13 (P.C.).

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.scheme_lacks_application_clause: The scheme contains no provision for applying to the court to alter, modify, or add to its terms.

issues.definition: If a management scheme lacks an application clause, it should be open to application for alteration, modification, or addition.

issues.legal_issue: An appellate court should not interfere with a discretionary costs order when it sees no reason to do so.
material_facts: The High Court allowed the deity, represented by its next friend, to recover a consolidated amount from the endowment for costs.
The appellant argued that costs should instead have been allowed on an attorney-and-client basis.
The Court considered the matter to be within the High Court's discretion and saw no reason to interfere.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the High Court's costs direction and made no order as to costs in the appeal.
issues.legal_principle: The form and amount of the costs recovery ordered by the High Court were matters within that court's discretion; the Court found no basis to disturb its decision.

predicates.appeal_reviewing_cost_order: An appeal challenges a costs order made by a lower court.
predicates.costs_order_within_lower_court_discretio: The challenged costs order concerns a matter entrusted to the lower court's discretion.
predicates.no_reason_to_interfere: The appellate court identifies no reason to disturb the lower court's discretionary decision.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a discretionary costs order and the appellate court finds no reason to interfere, the order remains undisturbed.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme need not determine disputes about transfer, inheritance, or termination of shebaitship where those rights may be challenged through remedies available at law.
material_facts: It was argued that shebaits transferred their turns to perform worship for consideration and that shebaitship was not transferable or heritable and ended on death.
The Court observed that shebaitship is a right in property.
The Court held that these matters did not require directions in the scheme and that a person challenging another's right to act as shebait could pursue an available legal remedy.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to require scheme directions on transferability, inheritance, or termination of shebaitship, leaving challenges to those rights to available remedies at law.
issues.legal_principle: Shebaitship is a right in property. A scheme need not resolve disputes about who is entitled to act as shebait; a person challenging that entitlement may pursue an available remedy at law.

predicates.management_scheme_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a court-settled scheme for managing a religious endowment.
predicates.challenge_concerns_shebaitship_transfer_: A challenge asks the court to regulate transfer of shebait functions or succession to the shebait role through the scheme.

issues.definition: In a management-scheme proceeding, a challenge concerning transfer or succession to shebaitship need not be decided in the scheme.

issues.legal_issue: A scheme amendment should not be disturbed when it makes no substantial difference to the provision it replaces.
material_facts: The appellant challenged the High Court's modification of a clause in the District Judge's scheme.
The Court compared the original and amended clauses and found no substantial difference between them.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to interfere with the High Court's modification of the clause.
issues.legal_principle: The Court found no substantial difference between the original and amended provisions and therefore saw no basis to disturb the amendment.

predicates.scheme_appeal: An appeal challenges a court-approved scheme for management of a religious endowment.
predicates.challenged_amendment_has_no_substantial_: The challenged amendment does not substantially change the provision it replaces.

issues.definition: When a scheme appeal challenges an amendment that makes no substantial difference, the amendment is not disturbed.
